tapeLine: Friday 23 October closed lower: S&P 500 -0.52% to 7,623.68, Nasdaq -0.21% to 25,955.34, Dow -1.23% (652.82 points) to 52,215.16, Russell 2000 -0.29% to 2,775.90, per the AP-style index recap (23 Oct). Monday futures levels were not found.
matters:
Oil, not tech, drove Friday: WTI crude rose above $100 a barrel on fears the U.S.-Iran conflict could flare again; energy was the only clear sector winner while consumer, telecom and financial shares lagged, per the 23 Oct index recap.

Tech steadied after Thursday’s sell-off: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 0.44% to 10,779.46. American Express fell more than 3% after announcing about 5% of its global workforce would be cut, per the same recap.

For the week the S&P 500 lost about 0.5%, the Nasdaq about 0.7% (a second straight weekly loss) and the Dow gained about 0.4%.

Invalidation: the S&P 500 closed below Tuesday’s 7,712.57 and about 2.4% under its 7,811.54 record close of 9 October; a close back above 7,712.57 would reverse that read.
alsoOnTape: Gold, Treasury yield and VIX levels were not found with a dated source and are not carried. WTI was reported above $100 on Friday; no exact settle was found.

regime.tag: The week ended with a rotation of pressure: Thursday’s tech sell-off paused (semiconductors +0.44%) but the Dow fell 1.23% as oil climbed above $100 on U.S.-Iran fears.
regime.sizing: The 27-28 October FOMC is the next scheduled catalyst; oil headlines are an unscheduled one.

secondOrder: The source of pressure changed within a day: Thursday’s weakness was AI-cost driven and hit the Nasdaq; Friday’s was energy-cost driven and hit the Dow. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The open question of whether the S&P 500 would reclaim Tuesday’s 7,712.57 was answered no: it closed Friday at 7,623.68, per the 23 Oct recap.
The prior brief’s framing of the Dow as the steady index (flat Thursday) did not carry: it fell 1.23% on Friday, the worst of the three.
The prior note that the sell-off was AI-cost specific held up in part: semiconductors stopped falling (+0.44%) once oil became the driver.
Whether yields kept falling after the PPI print still cannot be graded: no sourced yield levels were found.
The 27-28 October FOMC has not occurred.
